pages.text: A $(item)large battery$() catches fire from fire or lava beside it, a flint and steel, or lightning striking power wire that runs to it.$(br2)Once it is alight $(thing)nothing puts it out$(). It burns until it is used up, setting fire around it and spreading to the batteries it touches.

pages.title: Water
pages.text: Water against a burning battery holds the flames down: it hisses and steams, and stops spreading fire. It is still burning inside and keeps being used up. Take the water away before it is gone and it $(thing)flares up again$().

pages.title: Battery banks
pages.text: A battery that burns out in a group of $(thing)four or more$() touching batteries $(thing)explodes$(), harder the bigger the bank, and sets the rest of the bank alight. Some of those explosions start fires.$(br2)Keep banks small, keep them away from anything that burns, and keep fire and lava well away from them.
